items.title: Trump’s Super PAC to Pump $10 Million Into Texas to Boost Paxton
items.author: Bill Allison
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump’s super political action committee is spending $10 million to back Republican Ken Paxton’s US Senate bid in Texas, its biggest expenditure yet in this election cycle, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission.</article>

items.title: Nigel Farage’s Reform Hits Roadblocks in Quest for UK Power After Funding Sting
items.author: Lucy White, Katherine Griffiths and Jacob Reid
items.content: <article>Reform UK billed its 2026 conference as a showcase for policies it would implement during its first 100 days in power. In the end, the gathering served to highlight the mounting obstacles to Nigel Farage’s party winning office.</article>

items.title: Greek Premier Unveils €2.2 Billion in Economic Support for 2027
items.author: Sotiris Nikas
items.content: <article>Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis unveiled a package of economic measures worth €2.2 billion ($2.56 billion) in a bid to alleviate a cost of living crisis as the country gears up for national election next year.</article>

items.title: Vannacci, Italy’s Rising Right-Wing Star, Has Yet to Meet Meloni
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini and Chiara Albanese
items.content: <article>Italy’s Roberto Vannacci, the insurgent ultranationalist, has yet to meet Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni or have contact with her circle, as his rise begins to reshape her right-wing alliance before next year’s election.</article>

items.title: Portugal Sees No Threat to Schengen From Ceuta Migrant Surge
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini and Tiago Ramos Alfaro
items.content: <article>A surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta this summer didn’t pose a threat to the European Union’s free-travel zone, Portugal’s foreign minister said on Saturday.</article>

items.title: Spotify’s Lorentzon Says He’d Leave Sweden If Wealth Tax Imposed
items.author: Rafaela Lindeberg
items.content: <article>Spotify Technology SA co-founder Martin Lorentzon said he would leave Sweden immediately if the country introduces new wealth taxes, escalating concerns that proposals being debated ahead of this month’s election could drive entrepreneurs and capital abroad.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Embrace of AI Data Centers Adds to GOP’s Midterm Peril
items.author: Courtney Subramanian, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Steven T. Dennis
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump’s fervent support for artificial intelligence data centers has put him at odds with voters who increasingly oppose them and comes despite direct warnings that his stance threatens to deepen Republicans’ peril in the November midterm elections.</article>

items.title: US Strikes 3 Iranian Tankers in Retaliation for IRGC Attacks
items.author: Kevin Whitelaw
items.content: <article>The US military said it launched strikes against three Iranian crude oil tankers in retaliation for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeting two US Navy warships with ballistic missiles.</article>

items.title: German Police Secure Explosive Devices Targeting Power Grid
items.author: Christina Kyriasoglou and Eva Brendel
items.content: <article>Police in Germany discovered 12 explosive devices near overhead power lines in two districts in the country’s east, the latest in a spate of incidents targeting the country’s electricity infrastructure.</article>

items.title: Trump Oil Deal Blindsides US Energy Companies
items.content: <article>US oil executives say they were blindsided by the Trump administration’s Venezuela deal, which gives North American Blue Energy Partners access to fields that other companies had been pursuing. Bloomberg News White House Reporter Jennifer Dlouhy and Wall Street Journal National Security Reporter Vera Bergengruen are on Bloomberg This Weekend and say industry figures are also questioning whether the company can quickly develop new production and whether the arrangement can deliver lower gasoline prices before the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Missouri Asks US Supreme Court to Restore GOP-Backed Voting Map
items.author: Madlin Mekelburg
items.content: <article>Missouri and its Republican leaders asked the US Supreme Court to reinstate a congressional map engineered by GOP lawmakers in the state to favor the party in November’s midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Putin Orders No Airstrikes on Kyiv While US Envoys Visit
items.author: Ros Krasny
items.content: <article>Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered Kremlin troops not to fire on Kyiv for three days as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner prepare to visit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax.</article>

items.title: US Envoys Due in Kyiv After Putin Says Ending War ‘Not Simple’
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for more than three hours of talks in Moscow that a Kremlin aide called “highly useful,” setting the stage for the pair’s planned trip to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian leaders on Sunday.</article>

items.title: Kyiv Adapts to Constant Attack by Russian Jet-Powered Drones
items.author: Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova
items.content: <article>As a resident of Boryspil, a satellite town of Kyiv, Kostyantyn Kuts has grown accustomed to regular night-time air raids. This past week has been different.</article>

items.title: ‘We Can Only Win’: The Rise of the Far Right in Eastern Germany
items.author: Kamil Kowalcze
items.content: <article>In a village on the edge of Germany’s Harz mountains, families gathering at a beer-and-bratwurst summer picnic lined up for autographs and selfies from the man they want to lead the country’s first far-right state government since World War II.</article>

items.title: Burnham Gets His Own Breathing Space as Turmoil Engulfs Farage
items.author: Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>Andy Burnham was just starting to face awkward questions about his plans as Britain’s prime minster this week. Instead, his biggest rival, Nigel Farage, ended up being the one under greater pressure to explain.</article>

items.title: Tetris Distances Itself From White House’s Wall-Building Game
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>The maker of Tetris criticized a new White House digital game that mimics its classic puzzle by having players build a wall to stop migrants from crossing the US border.</article>

items.title: Xi’s Personnel Reshuffle Picks Up Pace as New Faces Emerge
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China has named a former vice finance minister as acting mayor of Shanghai, the latest in a string of appointments ahead of a key congress for the ruling Communist Party next year.</article>

items.title: Greek Premier Plans Fresh Economic Support as Election Nears
items.author: Sotiris Nikas
items.content: <article>Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is about to unveil an economic support package aimed at alleviating a cost of living crisis as he lays out his broader economic agenda ahead of next year’s national elections.</article>
